title: Ferenc Rákóczi II to an envoy bound for Holland, Lwów, 27 June 1711 (DECODE R483)

steps.what: Applied R639 to the Latin R483: nonsense, so a different key.
R483 found fully deciphered interlinearly at the time (Lwow, 27 June 1711, siege of Munkacs); key not rebuilt.
Fetched all 14 page images and re-transcribed every cipher page (R922, R912, R852, R483) with image-reading subagents; about 40% of DECODE lines corrected, two dropped lines restored.
Rebuilt the R483 syllabic key by hard-EM alignment of 168 cipher lines with the interlinear: 224 codes; key reproduces 70% of the clerk letters.

Entry split from rakoczi1704 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R483 is in its own Latin syllabary, not the R639 table of the three French letters. check483.py rerun after the move (69.9% clerk-letter agreement, output unchanged); interlinear coverage measured over tr/: 2,524 of 2,531 groups.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): tr/R483_p1-p6.txt, the clerk's decipherment R483_clerk.txt and the rebuilt-key decode R483_key_read.txt; key R483_key_rebuilt.json

outcome.method_basis: The clerk's contemporary interlinear decipherment covers 2,524 of the 2,531 cipher groups; it was transcribed and checked here against a 224-code key rebuilt from it by alignment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/rakoczi1711/tr/R483_p1-p6.txt: 2,524 of 2,531 cipher groups on lines with the clerk's interlinear (the other seven continue words written on the neighbouring line).
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from rakoczi1704, which keeps the three French letters in the R639 table. The rebuilt key reproduces 69.9% of the clerk's letters (3,180/4,547); 68 of its 224 codes occur once (grade C). DECODE date 7 June corrected to 27 June 1711.

credits.note: Clerk's interlinear decipherment of R483 (key rebuilt from it)

texts.label: R483, Lwów, 27 June 1711
texts.summary: Rákóczi's own Latin letter, signed 'Franciscus Princeps', to an envoy bound for Holland: he sends a copy of the 'Pax Caroliana' (Szatmár), which he calls a fraud engineered in Vienna, reports Archduke Charles proclaimed king in the Hungarian counties, and deals with money and the mathematical instruments ordered from Mangold. The text is the clerk's contemporary interlinear decipherment merged with the clear passages (R483_clerk.txt); R483_key_read.txt is the control decode with the key rebuilt here.

prior.where: contemporary interlinear decipherment over every ciphered stretch of the letter (DECODE R483 images)
